" * Returns a "sanitized" version of the string given as arguments, * where sanitized means non-printable characters have been * replaced with a question mark and the outcome is not longer * than 255 chars. * *

This method is used to clean up file names when they are * used in exception messages as they may end up in log files or * as console output and may have been read from a corrupted * input.

* * @param s the string to sanitize * @return a sanitized version of the argument * @since Compress 1.12 "

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- Failing test: ArchiveUtilsTest.sanitizeShortensString constructs a very long numeric string and asserts that ArchiveUtils.sanitize(input) returns a shortened version: the first 240 characters (4 full 60-char chunks) plus “012345678901” and an ellipsis “…”, totaling 255 characters. This verifies that sanitize should cap the output to 255 characters and append “…” if truncation occurs.

- Code under test: org.apache.commons.compress.utils.ArchiveUtils.sanitize(String) currently iterates over characters and replaces non-printable/SPECIALS with ‘?’, but it never enforces any maximum length or appends an ellipsis:
  - It builds the result in an unbounded StringBuilder and returns it directly.
  - Javadoc for this method explicitly promises “… the outcome is not longer than 255 chars.”

- Current bug report context: “Defective .zip-archive produces problematic error message” mentions a truncated zip causing an EOFException whose message contains a huge amount of byte[] data and overwhelms console logging. sanitize is meant to protect log/console output (per its Javadoc: “used to clean up file names when they are used in exception messages …”), including by capping length, but the current implementation doesn’t truncate, allowing excessively long content to pass through.

- Root cause: ArchiveUtils.sanitize(String) does not implement the documented and tested behavior of limiting the output length to 255 characters (with an ellipsis when truncated). This discrepancy causes the test sanitizeShortensString to fail and contributes to overly large error messages in the reported scenario.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
